title: Mastering A-Roll and B-Roll in Post-Production
body:
Editing a video can be so stressful. And when you really want your project to look really professional, you have to know how to use A-roll and B-roll.

This article talks about what they are and how to edit them together to make your work seem more put together.

What is an A-Roll?

An A-roll is the primary video. It provides the basis for the narrative of the video.

Examples of A-Roll: An interview, the host of the project, or the dialogue of the characters in a film.

Why it is important: An A-roll is what keeps your video together. Viewers watch your A-roll to learn what is going on in the video.

Problem: Your A-roll can get boring if you just have someone speaking for the entire duration of the video,

This is why we use a B-roll.

What is a B-Roll?

A B-roll is a secondary video. It provides background, color, or information to the A-roll.

Examples of a B-roll: Close ups of the subject, nature scenes, pictures, and action shots.

Why its important: A B-roll is what keeps your viewer from getting bored. While your A-roll speaks, your B-roll shows what is going on to keep your viewers from getting distracted.

Important to know: The audio of the B-roll gets muted or is removed completely. The viewers will hear the A-roll speak while a B-roll plays.

How to edit together your A-Roll and B-Roll?

Your video should flow very smoothly when you edit, here is some advice to do so.

Cut together your A-roll: Build your A-roll to tell your story with only the audio from your interviews or dialogue. Make sure you cut out any excess filler words or mistakes from your interview, leaving a clean version of your audio.

Watch out for your A-Rolls speaking: While watching your A-roll to cut, you should mark out the parts of your video where the speaker is describing something, moves onto a new topic, or when the video has a dragging part.

Cut your B-roll and edit them into your A-Roll: With your A-roll as the base of your video, you are going to edit your B-roll on top of it. Make sure that your B-roll provides a visual to what your A-roll is talking about.

Let the audio speak for itself: Make sure that your A-roll audio keeps playing as you watch your edited video with the B-roll to keep the audio flowing without any hiccups.

Simple tips for your edited video that should help it flow more smoothly

Make sure your Brolls lighting matches your A-Roll. Doing so will make your edited video look cohesive.

Don't add a B-roll everywhere. Let your viewers watch your speaker's face when they are saying something important or emotional.

Only add B-rolld that makes sense to what your A-roll is saying. Not everything needs to be accompanied by a B-roll.

By knowing how to use your A-roll and B-roll wisely, you can make your project go from a boring headshot video to a professional piece that keeps your viewers interested.
